policy_title: Introduce a £15 minimum wage and 10:1 pay ratio cap
stated: Introduce a minimum wage of £15 an hour for all ages, offsetting costs for small businesses by increasing the Employment Allowance to £10,000, and campaign for a maximum 10:1 pay ratio for all private and public-sector organisations.

source.quote: We will seek to introduce a minimum wage of £15 an hour for all, no matter your age, with the costs to small businesses offset by increasing the Employment Allowance to £10,000. Green MPs will campaign for a maximum 10:1 pay ratio for all private and public-sector organisations.

bearing_set.reason: Directly raises the pay floor for all workers and imposes a 10:1 pay ratio cap, affecting wage levels, pay equity, and job quality across the economy.

A higher minimum wage materially lifts disposable income for low-wage households (ability to afford essentials), while also carrying real contested inflationary risk through higher labour costs passed on as prices.

Both the minimum wage floor and the 10:1 pay ratio cap are explicitly designed to compress the pay distribution between bottom and top earners, directly moving the Gini and top-to-bottom gap indicators.

A very large minimum wage increase (approximately 31% above the current NLW for adults, far more for younger workers) has genuinely contested effects on employment levels, business formation and investment — real economic mechanisms that move O13's prosperity and opportunity indicators.
Doubling the Employment Allowance to £10,000 is a direct, concrete reduction in employer NIC receipts, materially affecting the funded/borrowed balance of public finances.

membership_note: Four bearings are warranted because the policy has distinct components each engaging a separate mechanism: wage-floor (O4), distributional compression (O14), contested employment/investment effects (O13), and a specific exchequer revenue cost via the Employment Allowance increase (O12).
